$comment: Who the traveller is actually contracting with. Every place the site names the company reads this file, because a legal entity typed into markup nine times is a legal entity that will be wrong in three of them.
$why: The tunnel now quotes a ground journey in US dollars and says the money goes to Wankong LLC. A visitor who reads that has one reasonable question — who is Wankong, I came here for Afrinkong — and the site could not answer it: the words 'Wankong LLC' appeared nowhere in the codebase, and the homepage footer said contact details were illustrative until verified. A price is only as trustworthy as the company behind it is identifiable.
relation: Afrinkong is a trading name of Wankong LLC.

office.$comment: The REGISTERED office, and labelled as one wherever it is printed. 8 The Green in Dover is a registered-agent address shared by a great many Delaware companies; it is the correct thing to publish as the company's registered office and it is not somewhere a traveller should be invited to visit, telephone or send anything. It is not an operating address and the site must never present it as one.

money: Journeys are quoted, invoiced and settled in US dollars, to Wankong LLC.
ground: The people who drive you, host you and coordinate your days are Afrinkong's own across Africa. The company you contract with and pay is Wankong LLC in the United States, which is what puts a US-registered business behind a journey run four thousand miles from it.

who.$comment: What the site says when a country has no operator of ours. The block it replaces said 'Not us, in Senegal' and 'Ask anyway' on roughly thirteen hundred pages. That copy was written to be scrupulously honest when the only product was three local operators, and it is now both weak and out of date: the ground journey is Afrinkong's own across all fifty-four countries. Opening the answer to 'who would take you' with who would not is a sentence that sells nothing and is no longer even true.
who.name: Afrinkong
who.say: The ground is ours right across Africa: your vehicle, your driver for the whole journey, and the days shaped around what you came for.
who.more: In Cameroon, Uganda and Namibia you travel with companies of our own as well.

enquiries.$comment: Where a journey built in the tunnel is sent. Until this existed there was nowhere for one to go: every enquiry on the site mailed bonjour@kamerun.cm, so a journey composed for Eritrea arrived at a Cameroonian operator's desk in Douala under a KAMERUN masthead with a +237 telephone number beside it. Kamerun keeps that address for Kamerun's own pages; this is Afrinkong's.
enquiries.$change_me: The mailbox is a placeholder consistent with the site's own canonical domain — every page already declares https://afrinkong.com — and the domain is not bought yet. It is one edit, here, and the tunnel, the enquiry page and the footer all follow it.
enquiries.say: Journeys are read by the Afrinkong coordination desk, which arranges the ground wherever the journey goes.
enquiries.hours: We answer within one working day.
